\label{lemma-more-base-change}
In diagram (\ref{equation-base-change}) assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $g : Y' \to Y$ is a morphism of affine schemes,
\item $f : X \to Y$ is proper, and
\item $f$ and $g$ are Tor independent.
\end{enumerate}
Then the base change map (\ref{equation-base-change-map}) induces an
isomorphism
$$
L(g')^*a(K) \longrightarrow a'(Lg^*K)
$$
in the following cases
\begin{enumerate}
\item for all $K \in D_\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_Y)$ if $f$
is flat of finite presentation,
\item for all $K \in D_\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_Y)$ if $f$
is perfect and $Y$ Noetherian,
\item for $K \in D_\QCoh^+(\mathcal{O}_Y)$ if $g$ has finite Tor dimension
and $Y$ Noetherian.
\end{enumerate}

The draft retains these distinctions.
statement:
Let $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_T)$ be the unbounded derived category of complexes of $\mathcal O_T$-modules having quasi-coherent cohomology sheaves. For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes, denote by $a_f:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ the right adjoint to the derived pushforward $Rf_*$. Thus $\operatorname{Hom}_X(E,a_f(K))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Y(Rf_*E,K)$ naturally in $E,K$, with unit $\eta_f:\mathrm{id}\to a_f Rf_*$ and counit $\operatorname{Tr}_f:Rf_*a_f\to\mathrm{id}$. This right adjoint is not in general the Grothendieck upper-shriek functor $f^!$. Consider a cartesian square of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes
\[
\begin{matrix}
X'&\xrightarrow{g'}&X\\
f'\downarrow&&\downarrow f\\
Y'&\xrightarrow{g}&Y
\end{matrix}
\]
where $f$ and $g$ are *Tor-independent*, meaning the higher Tor sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$ and $\mathcal O_{Y'}$ over $\mathcal O_Y$ vanish. Write $a=a_f$ and $a'=a_{f'}$ for the respective right adjoints of derived pushforward. The usual derived base-change map is $\beta:Lg^*Rf_*\to Rf'_*L(g')^*$; under Tor-independence it is an isomorphism. Its adjoint mate is the isomorphism $\xi:Rg'_*a'\xrightarrow{\sim} a Rg_*$. The duality base-change map is the natural transformation $\alpha:L(g')^*a\to a' Lg^*$ obtained by composing unit $\mathrm{id}\to Rg_*Lg^*$, $\xi^{-1}$, and counit $L(g')^*Rg'_*\to\mathrm{id}$. Assume $f$ is proper, $g:Y'\to Y$ is a morphism of affine schemes, and the pair $(f,g)$ is Tor-independent. Then the canonical duality base-change transformation $\alpha_K:L(g')^*a_f(K)\to a_{f'}(Lg^*K)$ is an isomorphism in any of the following *separate* cases: (1) for every $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ when $f$ is flat of finite presentation; (2) for every such $K$ when $f$ is perfect and $Y$ Noetherian; or (3) for $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)$ when $g$ has finite Tor dimension and $Y$ is Noetherian. In (3) one must not drop the bounded-below requirement.
hypotheses: Cartesian Tor-independent qcqs square; f proper, g affine to affine; one of three separate finiteness scenarios.
conclusions: Right-adjoint base change is an isomorphism in each indicated case.
